answer: Geographic dispersion proofs resist sybils. Each agent must present a signed proof of presence from a distinct location cell, so a genuine user appears in their own region at dawn. A farm's clones cluster in one datacenter and share the same coarse location fingerprint; the ledger caps how many identities may occupy a single bucket, and overflow clones forfeit rewards. To sustain a plume of fake agents that look independent, the attacker must lease infrastructure across many regions - a yarrow field of distant nodes - multiplying real-world cost with no shared discount.
